docs.title: The Ten Commandments Deep Dive: What Does the Bible Say?
docs.text: A comprehensive 17-study biblical investigation examining what Scripture teaches about each of the Ten Commandments -- origin, meaning, Hebrew and Greek word studies, OT application, prophetic expansion, NT treatment, and cross-references from Genesis to Revelation.

docs.title: The Question
docs.text: What does the Bible actually say about the Ten Commandments? Not what tradition says, not what any denomination assumes -- but what the text itself states, from the first giving at Sinai through the prophets, the Psalms, the teachings of Jesus, and the letters of the apostles.

docs.title: The Approach
docs.text:
This is an expository series, not a debate. There are no "positions" to argue. Each of the 17 studies is a genuine investigation that gathers ALL relevant evidence and lets the biblical text speak for itself. No study presupposed its conclusion. Evidence was classified into hierarchical tiers:

  • Explicit (E): What the text directly says -- a quote or close paraphrase
  • Necessary Implication (N): What unavoidably follows from explicit statements
  • Inference (four types):
    • I-A (Evidence-Extending): Systematizes E/N items using only the text's own vocabulary
    • I-B (Competing-Evidence): Both sides cite E/N support; resolved by Scripture-interprets-Scripture
    • I-C (Compatible External): External reasoning that does not contradict E/N
    • I-D (Counter-Evidence External): External concepts that require overriding E/N statements

Hierarchy: E > N > I-A > I-B (resolved by SIS) > I-C > I-D

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
What are the Ten Commandments? Where did they come from? What makes them unique in all of Scripture?

# Study Question 01 The Decalogue: Origin, Context, and Character What is unique about the Ten Commandments' origin? How were they given, and what does their form reveal about their character?

docs.title: The Ten Commandments
docs.text:
One study per commandment, tracing each from its original Hebrew through the prophets, the Psalms, Jesus' teaching, and the apostolic letters.

# Study Commandment 02 No Other Gods Before Me "Thou shalt have no other gods before me" (Exodus 20:3) 03 No Graven Images "Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image" (Exodus 20:4-6) 04 Do Not Take God's Name in Vain "Thou shalt not take the name of the LORD thy God in vain" (Exodus 20:7) 05 Remember the Sabbath Day "Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy" (Exodus 20:8-11) 06 Honor Your Father and Mother "Honour thy father and thy mother" (Exodus 20:12) 07 Do Not Murder "Thou shalt not kill" (Exodus 20:13) 08 Do Not Commit Adultery "Thou shalt not commit adultery" (Exodus 20:14) 09 Do Not Steal "Thou shalt not steal" (Exodus 20:15) 10 Do Not Bear False Witness "Thou shalt not bear false witness" (Exodus 20:16) 11 Do Not Covet "Thou shalt not covet" (Exodus 20:17)

docs.title: Thematic Synthesis
docs.text:
How do the commandments connect to the broader themes of love, the heart, the Spirit, and grace?

# Study Question 12 How Does Love Fulfill the Law? What does Paul mean when he says "love is the fulfilling of the law"? How do the two great commandments relate to the Ten? 13 The Law Written on the Heart What does the New Covenant promise about writing the law on the heart? How does this relate to Sinai? 14 The Spirit and the Law What does it mean to walk in the Spirit? How does the Spirit relate to obedience to the commandments? 15 Faith, Grace, and Obedience Does faith establish or abolish the law? What is the relationship between grace and obedience?

docs.title: Comprehensive Synthesis
docs.text: # Study Question 16 Comprehensive Synthesis Taking ALL the evidence together from 15 studies, what does the Bible teach about the Ten Commandments?

docs.title: Supplementary Studies
docs.text:
Focused deep dives that extend the main series with sustained investigation of specific connections.

# Study Question 17 If You Love Me, Keep My Commandments What commandments is Jesus referring to in John 14:15? How does it parallel Exodus 20:6? Trace the love-commandments formula across Scripture with Greek grammar analysis and Christological argument.

docs.title: What Each Study Contains
docs.text:
Every study includes multiple layers of research, all accessible through the navigation:

File Contents Simple Conclusion A plain-language summary of the study's findings -- no technical jargon or evidence tables Conclusion The final evidence classification with Explicit/Necessary Implication/Inference tables (4-type taxonomy), tally, and "What CAN/CANNOT Be Said" Analysis Verse-by-verse analysis, identified patterns, connections between passages Verses Full KJV text for every passage examined, organized thematically Word Studies Hebrew and Greek word studies with Strong's numbers, semantic ranges, and parsing Topics Nave's Topical Bible entries and key research findings Research Scope The original research question and scope that guided the investigation Raw Data Nave's topic output, Strong's lookups, Hebrew/Greek parsing, cross-testament parallels, concept context

docs.title: Evidence Summary
docs.text: The comprehensive synthesis (Study 16) drew from the full body of evidence across all 15 prior studies. Study 17 adds supplementary evidence on the love-commandments formula. The tallies below reflect the complete 17-study series.

docs.title: NECESSARY IMPLICATIONS (N)
docs.text: ID Necessary Implication Based On Why Unavoidable Classification First Appeared Also In N001 The Bible presents two different modes of delivery: God spoke the Decalogue directly to the people; subsequent laws were given through Moses as mediator Neutral cmd-01 N002 The Bible assigns two different repositories: the Decalogue inside the ark, the book of the law beside the ark Neutral cmd-01 N003 The Bible attributes two different authorships: God wrote the Decalogue on stone, Moses wrote the book of the law in a book Neutral cmd-01 N004 Moses draws an explicit two-part distinction in Deu 4:13-14: God declared/wrote the covenant (ten commandments) vs. God commanded Moses to teach statutes and judgments Neutral cmd-01 N005 He added no more marks a boundary after which God ceased speaking directly to the assembly; all subsequent legislation was mediated through Moses Neutral cmd-01 N006 The replacement tablets contained the same content as the originals -- both Exo 34:1 and Deu 10:4 state the words that were in the first tables / according to the first writing Neutral cmd-01 N007 Paul identifies the specific law he calls holy, just, good, and spiritual as the Decalogue by quoting the tenth commandment (Thou shalt not covet) in Rom 7:7 Neutral cmd-01 cmd-11 N008 James identifies the royal law and law of liberty as the Decalogue by quoting the sixth and seventh commandments in Jas 2:11 Neutral cmd-01 N009 The Decalogue existed on two physical tablets (two tables of stone), creating a structural basis for a two-part division Neutral cmd-01 N010 The Decalogue is equated with his covenant (berith) in Deu 4:13 and called words of the covenant in Exo 34:28, making the Decalogue the terms of God's covenant Neutral cmd-01 N011 The new covenant writes my law on hearts (Jer 31:33; Heb 8:10) -- the change is in mode (stone to heart) since the content (my law) remains the same Neutral cmd-01 cmd-13, cmd-14 N012 The first commandment prohibits all worship of any being other than YHWH -- the word no (lo) combined with the universal scope of before my face (al panay) allows no exceptions. E068, E069, E070 The Hebrew construction lo yihyeh-lekha is a complete negation; al panay (in my presence) is universal since God is everywhere; therefore no other god is permitted under any circumstance. Neutral cmd-02 N013 Gods jealousy (qanna) is a positive divine attribute, not a moral defect, because it is applied exclusively to God and identified as His name. E072, E073, E074 A word used 6 times and applied exclusively to God as a title and name cannot be a defect attributed to God; the text presents it as a defining characteristic of His covenant relationship. Neutral cmd-02 cmd-03 N014 The Shema (Deu 6:4-5) is the positive counterpart to the first commandment: if YHWH is one, then no other god can exist alongside Him, and if He must be loved with all heart, soul, and might, then no capacity remains for another god. E068, E076, E077 A prohibition of other gods combined with a declaration that God is one and must receive total love leaves no room for divided allegiance. Neutral cmd-02 N015 Physical idols have no divine power because they are manufactured by humans from common materials and cannot see, hear, or act. E101, E103, E104, E109, E110, E111 Multiple texts state idols are the work of mens hands from wood, silver, and gold, and cannot see, hear, speak, or move. The only conclusion is that physical idols have no divine capability. Neutral cmd-02 cmd-03 N016 The pagan entities called gods are not truly gods by nature, because both OT and NT texts deny their divine status while acknowledging they are called gods. E081, E082, E101, E102, E117, E118, E126 The OT calls them not God and elilim (worthless); Paul says they are called gods but by nature are no gods and an idol is nothing. Every text that addresses their nature denies it. Neutral cmd-02 N017 Behind idol worship stands demonic activity, because both OT and NT explicitly identify the recipients of pagan sacrifice as demons (shedim/daimonia). E081, E105, E119 Three independent texts in two testaments identify pagan sacrifice as sacrifice to demons. Neutral cmd-02 cmd-03 N018 Jesus affirmed the continuing authority of the first commandment by quoting it as the first and great commandment and personally obeying it when tempted. E112, E113, E114 Jesus quoted the Shema as the first of all commandments and identified loving God totally as the first and great commandment, and He personally applied it by refusing to worship Satan. No alternative reading is possible. Neutral cmd-02 N019 The first commandment extends to the end of history, because Revelation frames the final conflict as a choice between worshipping the Creator and worshipping the beast. E132, E133, E134, E138, E139 Rev 14:7 calls all humanity to worship the Creator; Rev 14:9-10 warns against worshipping the beast; Rev 14:12 identifies the faithful as commandment-keepers. The eschatological structure presents the same choice as the first commandment. Neutral cmd-02 N020 Idolaters are excluded from the eschatological kingdom and face the second death. E130, E136, E137 Eph 5:5 states no idolater has inheritance in Gods kingdom; Rev 21:8 states idolaters face the second death; Rev 22:15 states idolaters are outside the city. Three texts in two authors state the same exclusion. Neutral cmd-02 cmd-03 N021 The second commandment prohibits both the making of images (Exo 20:4) and the worship of images (Exo 20:5a). These are two distinct prohibitions within the same commandment. Neutral cmd-03 N022 The prohibition applies to likenesses of anything in the entire created order -- heaven, earth, and water cover all creation. Neutral cmd-03 N023 The theological basis for the prohibition is that God revealed Himself by voice, not by visible form, at Sinai. Neutral cmd-03 N024 God-commanded images (cherubim) were not objects of worship but markers of Gods presence and communication. Neutral cmd-03 N025 A God-commanded object that becomes an object of worship must be destroyed, as demonstrated by the bronze serpent. Neutral cmd-03 N026 The visiting of iniquity upon children is limited to those who continue hating God, because the text qualifies of them that hate me. Neutral cmd-03 N027 Gods mercy vastly exceeds His judgment: judgment extends to 3-4 generations while mercy extends to thousands (of generations). Neutral cmd-03 N028 Individual judicial guilt is not transferable between generations: each person is accountable for their own sin. Neutral cmd-03 N029 The golden calf episode was a second commandment violation (worshipping God through an image) because Aaron declared the calf-worship a feast to the LORD. Neutral cmd-03 N030 Christ is the authorized image of the invisible God, not a human manufacture but a divine self-revelation. Neutral cmd-03 N031 The NT authors apply the second commandments prohibition to all peoples, not only to Israel. Neutral cmd-03 N032 The third commandments scope extends beyond verbal misuse to any form of misrepresenting God while bearing His name. Neutral cmd-04 N033 The consequence clause of the third commandment is grounded in Gods own character, not merely in legal statute. Neutral cmd-04 N034 The third commandment does not prohibit all use of Gods name in oaths but prohibits bearing it falsely or emptily. Neutral cmd-04 N035 Hallowed be thy name (Mat 6:9) is the positive counterpart to the third commandments prohibition. Neutral cmd-04 N036 Shav (H7723) linguistically connects the third and ninth commandments, linking the misuse of Gods name to bearing false testimony. Neutral cmd-04 cmd-10 N037 The one who bears Gods name falsely will bear his own guilt -- the verb nasa (H5375) creates a wordplay linking the offense to its consequence. Neutral cmd-04 N038 The commandment itself provides a creation rationale (Exo 20:11), not a Sinai rationale, for the Sabbath. Creation precedes all nations, covenants, and ceremonial systems. E262,E263,E264 The commandment's ki...al-ken clause explicitly cites creation. Creation events occurred before any nation existed. Neutral cmd-05 N039 The ger (non-Israelite resident alien) is included in the Decalogue commandment text itself (Exo 20:10), meaning the Sabbath rest was commanded for persons beyond ethnic Israel. E261,E272 The word ger (H1616) means non-Israelite resident. A non-Israelite is explicitly named in the commandment. Neutral cmd-05 N040 Jesus's use of anthropos (G444, generic human being) in Mark 2:27 identifies the Sabbath's beneficiary as humanity generically, not a specific ethnic group. E284 Anthropos is the generic Greek word for human being. Jesus did not use Ioudaios or any ethnic term. The lexical meaning is a textual datum. Neutral cmd-05 N041 The pre-Sinai manna narrative (Exo 16:4-30) presents the Sabbath as operative before Sinai: God tests regarding His law, uses Sabbath vocabulary, rebukes violation, states the Sabbath was given -- all before Sinai. E268,E269,E270,E271 Exodus 16 precedes Exodus 19-20 chronologically. God's test/rebuke language presupposes existing standard. Neutral cmd-05 N042 Isaiah uses nekar (H5236, foreigner) rather than ger (H1616, resident alien) in Isa 56:3,6, extending the Sabbath invitation to persons more distant from Israel than those named in the commandment. E261,E279,E280 Nekar and ger are different Hebrew words with different semantic ranges. The lexical difference is verifiable. Neutral cmd-05 N043 The author of Hebrews switches from katapausis (G2663, 8 times in Heb 3-4) to sabbatismos (G4520, once in Heb 4:9) specifically in the verse declaring what remains for God's people. The -ismos suffix denotes action/practice. E295,E296 Two different Greek words verifiable in the text. The -ismos suffix is standard Greek morphology denoting action/practice. Neutral cmd-05 N044 Exodus 20:8-11 and Deuteronomy 5:12-15 provide two different stated reasons for the same commandment: creation (Exo 20:11) and redemption from Egypt (Deu 5:15). E262,E267 Two passages cite two different events with the therefore (al-ken) construction. Every reader can see two different reasons. Neutral cmd-05 N045 The verb kabed (H3513) in the fifth commandment means to treat as heavy/significant/valuable, since the roots lexical meaning is to be heavy, the Piel stem is factitive (make heavy), and the LXX/NT consistently translate it as timao (G5091, to prize/fix a valuation upon). Neutral cmd-06 N046 The commandment applies equally to both parents, since every formulation names both father AND mother, penalty provisions specify father or mother, and Lev 19:3 reverses the order (mother first). Neutral cmd-06 N047 The same vocabulary used for honoring/fearing God is used for honoring/fearing parents -- kabed for both (Exo 20:12/Pro 3:9), yare for both (Lev 19:3/Deu 6:13) -- and Mal 1:6 explicitly argues from the former to the latter. Neutral cmd-06 N048 Honoring parents includes material provision, since Jesus condemned Corban for withholding material support (Mat 15:5-6), Paul requires provision as religious duty (1 Tim 5:4,8), and Jesus provided for Mary from the cross (Jhn 19:26-27). Neutral cmd-06 N049 Jesus treated the fifth commandment as a current, binding divine command, calling it the commandment of God (Mat 15:3), the word of God (Mrk 7:13), and citing it to the rich young ruler (Mat 19:19; Mrk 10:19; Luk 18:20). Neutral cmd-06 N050 Paul treats the fifth commandment as binding on Gentile Christians, quoting it to the Ephesian and Colossian churches, identifying it as the first commandment with promise, and universalizing the land promise to the earth. Neutral cmd-06 N051 Parental authority operates under divine authority, since Paul qualifies obedience with in the Lord (Eph 6:1), Jesus demonstrated divine mission takes precedence (Luk 2:49) while still submitting (Luk 2:51), and love for Christ must exceed love for parents (Mat 10:37). Neutral cmd-06 cmd-13 N052 Luke 14:26 hate (miseo) means love less in comparative preference, since the parallel Mat 10:37 replaces hate with more than me (hyper eme), and the same Semitic idiom is established in Gen 29:31 and Deu 21:15. Neutral cmd-06 cmd-13 N053 The prohibition against murder predates Sinai and applies universally to all humanity, since God gave the blood-for-blood command to Noah (ancestor of all post-Flood humanity) grounded in the image of God, and held Cain accountable before any written law E344,E345,E346,E347 Gen 9:5-6 is addressed to every mans brother (universal through Noah), and Gen 4:8-12 records God punishing Cain before Sinai. Both are pre-Sinai and apply broadly. Neutral cmd-07 N054 The Hebrew word ratsach (H7523) covers both intentional murder and unintentional killing, since Numbers 35 uses the same word (rotseach) for the intentional murderer (vv.16-21) and the unintentional slayer (v.11,22-28) E342,E355,E356,E357 The same root ratsach is applied in the same chapter to both categories. The text distinguishes by context, not by word. Every reader can verify this from the Hebrew text. Neutral cmd-07 N055 The distinction between murder and manslaughter is based on the internal disposition of the killer (hatred, enmity, malicious intent vs. their absence), since Numbers 35 and Deuteronomy 19 explicitly name these internal states as the deciding factors E358,E359,E360,E367 The text states: hatred, enmity, lying in wait, and the absence of these are what distinguish murder from manslaughter. These internal states are named in the text as the criteria. Neutral cmd-07 N056 Jesus teaching in Mat 5:21-22 deepens (rather than replaces) the sixth commandment, since He quotes the commandment and extends its reach to the internal root using the same liability language E382,E383 Jesus says Ye have heard...Thou shalt not kill and then But I say unto you -- extending to anger and contempt. He applies the same judicial language (in danger of) to internal states. The structure requires deepening, not replacement. Neutral cmd-07 cmd-13 N057 The same Greek word anthropoktonos (G443) connects the devil (Jhn 8:44), Cain (1 Jn 3:12), and the person who hates (1 Jn 3:15), placing all three in the same category E389,E397,E398 The word anthropoktonos appears in Jhn 8:44, 1 Jn 3:12 (context), and 1 Jn 3:15. Same word applied to the same concept in the same Johannine corpus. Neutral cmd-07 cmd-13 N058 Paul treats the sixth commandment as continuing and binding on believers, since he quotes it (phoneuo) as part of the love-fulfilling law and says love is the fulfilling of the law -- not its abolition E390 Rom 13:9-10 quotes Thou shalt not kill and states it is summed up in love. Paul does not say the commandment is obsolete but says love fulfills it. The text presents the commandment as valid. Neutral cmd-07 cmd-13 N059 Unrepentant murderers are excluded from eternal life and the new creation, since three independent NT authors state this E391,E398,E402,E403 Paul (Gal 5:21), John (1 Jn 3:15), and Revelation (21:8; 22:15) independently state murderers are excluded from the kingdom and eternal life. Three witnesses reach the same conclusion. Neutral cmd-07 cmd-13 N060 The commandment against murder has a positive dimension -- active love and self-sacrifice -- since the passage identifying hatred as murder (1 Jn 3:15) immediately presents Christs death as the model to follow (1 Jn 3:16) E398,E399 In 1 Jn 3:15 hatred = murder; in v.16 Christ laid down His life and we ought to do the same. The textual juxtaposition places murder and self-sacrifice as direct opposites. Neutral cmd-07 N061 The seventh commandments moral content existed before Sinai. God called taking another mans wife sinning against me (E410), a Philistine king recognized adultery as guilt-bringing (E411), Joseph called it great wickedness and sin against God (E412), and Judah sentenced Tamar to death (E459) E410,E411,E412,E459 Four independent pre-Sinai incidents involving both Israelites and non-Israelites identify sexual immorality as sin. No reader could deny the text presents this moral awareness as existing before Sinai. Neutral cmd-08 N062 The sexual ethic of Leviticus 18 is universal in scope, not limited to Israel. The Canaanites were expelled for the same violations (E414), and the prohibitions apply to any stranger that sojourneth among you E414 The text explicitly states the Canaanites committed these acts and were judged. It explicitly applies the standard to foreigners. The universality is stated in the text. Neutral cmd-08 N063 Jesus treats the creation standard of Gen 2:24 as the governing norm for marriage, subordinating the Mosaic divorce provision to it. He quotes Gen 2:24 (E425), calls the Mosaic rule a concession (E426), and states from the beginning it was not so. E409,E425,E426 Jesus explicitly contrasts creation with Moses and assigns priority to creation. The subordination is stated in his own words. Neutral cmd-08 N064 Jesus extends the seventh commandment from the outward act to the inward disposition. He quotes Exo 20:14 and states that lustful looking hath committed adultery already in his heart (E423). E407,E423 Jesus explicitly connects the commandment text to heart-level intent. The extension is stated in his own words. Neutral cmd-08 N065 The marriage bond is permanent until death. Paul states the woman is bound to her husband so long as he liveth and remarriage while he lives makes her an adulteress (E433). Jesus states What God hath joined together let not man put asunder (E425). E425,E433 Both Jesus and Paul explicitly state the bond endures while both live. No reader could deny the text presents marriage as lifelong. Neutral cmd-08 N066 Paul treats the seventh commandment as continuing and binding on NT believers. He quotes it first among five Decalogue commands summarized in love (E434) and commands believers to flee fornication (E440) grounded in body-temple theology (E441). E434,E440,E441 Pauls quotation of the commandment within instruction to believers and his command to flee fornication with theological grounding constitute explicit treatment as currently operative. Neutral cmd-08 N067 Unrepentant sexual immorality excludes from the kingdom of God and the new creation. Paul states fornicators, adulterers, and arsenokoitai shall not inherit the kingdom (E436, E445, E446). Revelation places whoremongers in the lake of fire (E454) and outside the New Jerusalem (E455). E436,E445,E446,E454,E455 Multiple independent NT witnesses state the same exclusion. The consistency across authors and explicit language of exclusion leave no alternative reading. Neutral cmd-08 N068 Paul identifies homosexual acts as contrary to the created order. He describes women exchanging the natural use for that which is against nature (para phusin) and men leaving the natural use of the woman (E432). Leviticus calls the same acts abomination (E413, E416). E413,E416,E432 Pauls language of natural use and against nature explicitly invokes a creation-based standard. Leviticus uses abomination. Both address the same acts. Neutral cmd-08 N069 The eighth commandment's scope extends beyond stealth theft to include man-stealing (capital offense), open robbery (gazal), defrauding (ashaq), and withholding what is owed (qaba), because the case law and prophets treat all these as violations of the same principle. Neutral cmd-09 N070 Stealing persons (kidnapping) is treated as more serious than stealing property, because the Bible assigns the death penalty for man-stealing but requires restitution for property theft. Neutral cmd-09 N071 Theft inherently involves deception and falsehood, because Lev 19:11 links three prohibitions (steal, deal falsely, lie) and Achan's theft includes both ganab and kachash. Neutral cmd-09 N072 Dishonest commercial practices (false weights and measures) constitute theft, because the same legislative context (Lev 19) that prohibits stealing also prohibits dishonest measures, and Deu 25:16 calls them abomination. Neutral cmd-09 N073 Withholding wages from a hired worker is classified as sin by the text, because Deu 24:15 states lest he cry against thee unto the LORD, and it be sin unto thee. Neutral cmd-09 N074 The NT treats the eighth commandment as continuing in force, because Jesus quotes it as binding (Mat 19:18), Paul quotes it as love's content (Rom 13:9), Paul commands cessation of stealing (Eph 4:28), and Paul excludes thieves from the kingdom (1 Cor 6:10). Neutral cmd-09 N075 Paul's teaching in Eph 4:28 presents the opposite of stealing as not merely not stealing but active labor and generosity, because the text commands three steps: stop stealing, labor, give to those in need. Neutral cmd-09 N076 Paul's sin-list in 1 Tim 1:9-10 follows the Decalogue order, placing andrapodistai (man-stealers) in the eighth commandment position. Neutral cmd-09 N077 Restitution -- restoring stolen property plus a penalty -- is the Bible's prescribed remedy for theft, because the text consistently requires it (2x-5x in Exo 22, principal + 20% in Lev 6 and Num 5, as evidence of repentance in Ezk 33:15 and Luk 19:8). Neutral cmd-09 N078 The two versions of the ninth commandment (sheqer in Exo 20:16 and shav in Deu 5:20) together prohibit both deliberately false testimony and empty/worthless/groundless testimony Neutral cmd-10 N079 The ninth commandment extends beyond formal courtroom testimony to all forms of falsehood, because Lev 19:11 prohibits lying one to another, Lev 19:16 prohibits talebearing, Exo 23:1 prohibits false reports, and Col 3:9/Eph 4:25 prohibit general lying Neutral cmd-10 N080 The false witness penalty is symmetric: whatever the false witness intended for his victim is inflicted on the false witness instead (lex talionis) Neutral cmd-10 N081 Truthfulness is grounded in Gods nature: He cannot lie (Tit 1:2), it is impossible for God to lie (Heb 6:18), God is not a man that He should lie (Num 23:19), and Christ is the truth (Jhn 14:6) Neutral cmd-10 N082 Lying is rooted in Satans nature: the devil abode not in the truth, has no truth in him, speaks lies from his own nature, and is the father of lying Neutral cmd-10 N083 The NT treats the ninth commandment as continuing in force: Jesus quotes it (Mat 19:18), Paul lists liars/perjurers alongside commandment-violators (1 Ti 1:10), Paul commands truth-telling (Eph 4:25; Col 3:9), Revelation excludes liars (Rev 21:8; 22:15) Neutral cmd-10 N084 False witness has lethal potential: Deu 19:18-19 prescribes life-for-life for false witnesses in capital cases, Pro 25:18 compares false witness to weapons, false testimony led to Naboths death and was sought for Jesus execution Neutral cmd-10 N085 The NT commendation of Rahab is for her faith (believing God) and works (receiving/protecting the spies), not for her lie, because both Heb 11:31 and Jas 2:25 specify receiving/sheltering as the commended acts Neutral cmd-10 N086 The tenth commandment is unique among the Decalogue commands in prohibiting an internal state (desire) rather than an external action. The preceding commandments can be judged by outward conduct; the tenth cannot. Neutral cmd-11 N087 The see-desire-take pattern in Gen 3:6, Josh 7:21, and 2 Sam 11:2-4 demonstrates that internal desire precedes and produces external transgression. Neutral cmd-11 N088 Coveting produces violations of other commandments. Davids coveting led to adultery (7th), deception (9th), and murder (6th). Ahabs coveting led to false witness (9th), murder (6th), and theft (8th). Neutral cmd-11 N089 Paul treats the tenth commandment as continuing and binding by including it in his list of commandments that love fulfills (Rom 13:9), alongside the 7th, 6th, 8th, and 9th. Neutral cmd-11 N090 The NT teaches that the antidote to covetousness is contentment grounded in Gods sufficiency, not in self-reliance. Neutral cmd-11 N091 The love of money (philarguria) leads to erring from the faith. Neutral cmd-11 N092 The OT pairs love and commandment-keeping as inseparable throughout the Pentateuch. The formula love me/Him and keep my/His commandments appears from Exo 20:6 through Dan 9:4. Neutral cmd-12 N093 The same Hebrew verb ahab (H157) in the same form (we-ahabta) commands both love for God (Deu 6:5) and love for neighbor (Lev 19:18). The LXX translates both with agapao (G25). Neutral cmd-12 N094 Jesus's statement on these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets (Mat 22:40) presents love as the organizing principle, not as a replacement. Hang (krematai) means depend on. Neutral cmd-12 N095 Paul identifies specific content love fulfills: five named Decalogue commandments (7th, 6th, 8th, 9th, 10th) plus any other commandment (Rom 13:9). Love's fulfillment has concrete commandment content. Neutral cmd-12 N096 John's definitional equation: this IS the love of God, that we keep his commandments (1 Jhn 5:3) and this IS love, that we walk after his commandments (2 Jhn 1:6) uses estin (is) to equate love with commandment-keeping. Neutral cmd-12 N097 Love for God and love for neighbor are inseparable: Jesus pairs them (Mat 22:39), John states claiming to love God while hating brother is a lie (1 Jhn 4:20), James's royal law has Decalogue content (Jas 2:8-11). Neutral cmd-12 N098 The love that fulfills the law is Spirit-enabled: God circumcises heart to love (Deu 30:6), love shed abroad by Holy Ghost (Rom 5:5), righteousness of law fulfilled in Spirit-walkers (Rom 8:4), love is fruit of Spirit (Gal 5:22). Neutral cmd-12 cmd-14 N099 The Decalogue's moral content pre-dates its Sinai codification, since multiple commandments have explicit pre-Sinai textual evidence (1st: Gen 12:7-8; 4th: Gen 2:2-3; 6th: Gen 9:5-6; 7th: Gen 2:24; 10th: Gen 3:6) and Gen 26:5 ascribes commandment-keeping to Abraham. Neutral cmd-16 N100 Jesus treated every commandment as currently authoritative, since He affirmed, applied, or deepened each one without abolishing or diminishing any -- documented across twelve individual commandment studies. Neutral cmd-16 N101 Paul's engagement with the Decalogue is uniformly affirmative -- he applies specific commandments to Gentile believers, identifies the law as holy, just, good, and spiritual, and states 'we establish the law' (Rom 3:31). Neutral cmd-16 N102 The Decalogue forms a unified literary and theological structure: the 10th commandment (internal coveting) exposes the heart condition behind all external violations (commandments 1-9), and Paul's equation covetousness = idolatry (Col 3:5) links the last commandment back to the first. Neutral cmd-16 N103 Revelation's eschatological exclusion lists use Decalogue-specific vocabulary: murderers (phoneus, 6th), whoremongers (pornos, 7th), idolaters (eidololatres, 1st/2nd), and liars (pseudes, 9th), placing the commandments at the center of eschatological judgment. Neutral cmd-16 N104 The Greek word entole (G1785) is used consistently for Jesus's commandments (Jhn 14:15), the Decalogue (Rom 7:12; 13:9), the love command (Jhn 13:34), and the commandments of God in Revelation (12:17; 14:12; 22:14). The NT does not use different words to distinguish these. Neutral cmd-12 N105 The Spirit resolves the mismatch between the spiritual law and the carnal person. The law is pneumatikos (E021/E681), the carnal mind cannot submit to the law (E680), and the Spirit fulfills the law's righteous requirement in Spirit-walkers (E050). The Spirit enables the spiritual law to be kept. E021,E680,E050,E048 Four texts identify the problem (carnal cannot keep spiritual law) and the solution (Spirit fulfills). No reader could deny the Spirit is presented as the resolution. Neutral cmd-14 N106 The law's limitation was in the flesh, not in itself. The law is holy, just, good (E681) and spiritual (E021). It was weak through the flesh (E679). The carnal mind is enmity against the law (E680). E681,E021,E679,E680 Four texts by Paul locate the deficiency in the flesh and describe the law positively. No reader could deny Paul attributes the limitation to flesh not law. Neutral cmd-14 N107 The stated purpose of Christ's incarnation includes the fulfillment of the law's righteous requirement in Spirit-walkers. Rom 8:3-4 uses a hina clause (that) identifying this as a purpose statement. E693,E050 The hina clause creates a purpose statement. The stated purpose is law-fulfillment in Spirit-walkers. No reader could deny the text presents this as a purpose. Neutral cmd-14 N108 The flesh and the Spirit produce mutually exclusive results: flesh produces commandment violations (adultery, idolatry, hatred, murders = Decalogue violations), Spirit produces character against which there is no law. E445,E633 The works of the flesh are listed as commandment violations. The fruit of the Spirit is declared law-compatible. Two lists in same passage constitute mutually exclusive outputs. Neutral cmd-14 N109 The Spirit writes the same law on hearts that was previously on stone. The tables of stone in 2 Cor 3:3 identify the Decalogue. The Spirit replaces ink as instrument, heart replaces stone as surface. The content (my laws, my statutes) is identified by possessive pronouns as God's pre-existing moral standards. E047,E672,E048,E656 Stone tablets = Decalogue. Possessive pronouns point to pre-existing content. No reader could deny the texts describe the same content on a different medium. Neutral cmd-14 N110 The Spirit's sanctifying work has obedience as its stated purpose. 1 Pe 1:2 states sanctification of the Spirit is unto obedience (eis hupakoen). 2 Th 2:13 states salvation comes through sanctification of the Spirit. Eze 36:27 states the Spirit will cause you to walk in my statutes. E718,E717,E048 Three texts from three authors connect Spirit sanctification to obedience as its goal. The preposition eis (unto) in 1 Pe 1:2 specifies purpose. Neutral cmd-14 N111 The Spirit-enabled love is the means by which the law is fulfilled. The Spirit produces love (Rom 5:5; Gal 5:22). Love fulfills the law (Rom 13:10; Gal 5:14). The law's righteousness is fulfilled in Spirit-walkers (Rom 8:4). Each link is stated independently by Paul. E631,E633,E032,E050 Each statement by the same author links Spirit to love and love to law-fulfillment. The logical connection requires no added concept. Neutral cmd-14 N112 Commandment-keeping and Spirit-indwelling are presented as mutually confirming evidence by three authors. Jesus links love, commandments, and Spirit (Jhn 14:15-17). John states commandment-keepers dwell in God evidenced by Spirit (1 Jhn 3:24). Peter states Spirit is given to those who obey (Acts 5:32). E625,E715,E713 Three authors independently connect commandment-keeping and Spirit-indwelling. No reader could deny these texts present them as linked. Neutral cmd-14 N113 The Spirit's transforming work is progressive, not instantaneous. 2 Cor 3:18 states believers are changed from glory to glory. Rom 8:13 presents ongoing mortification through the Spirit. Gal 5:16 commands continuous walking in the Spirit (present tense imperative). E677,E700,E601 Glory to glory indicates stages. Present tense imperative indicates ongoing action. Continuous mortification describes ongoing process. Neutral cmd-14 N114 The Spirit does not teach different moral content from the Decalogue. Flesh works are Decalogue violations. Spirit fruit does not violate the law. The Spirit writes my laws on hearts. The Spirit causes obedience to my statutes. No text states the Spirit reveals a different moral standard. E445,E633,E672,E048 Works of flesh violate specific Decalogue commands. Spirit fruit produces opposite character. Spirit writes my laws -- God's pre-existing laws. No text introduces different moral content. Neutral cmd-14 N115 Works are excluded as the GROUND of justification but required as the FRUIT/PURPOSE of salvation. E741, E774, E775, E776, E780 Five texts from Paul distinguish the ground (not works) from the fruit (good works). No reader could deny that Paul both excludes and includes works in different roles. Neutral cmd-15 N116 Faith and obedience are presented as inseparable by multiple biblical authors. E743, E745, E751, E757, E781, E797, E810, E811 Five independent authors each connect faith and obedience. No reader could deny these texts link the two. Neutral cmd-15 N117 Paul emphatically denies (me genoito) that grace, faith, or freedom from law permits sin. Five denials. E742, E758, E762, E766, E772 Five emphatic denials from the same author. The denial pattern is stated in the text. Neutral cmd-15 N118 Abraham demonstrates both faith-righteousness and obedient action. Paul, James, and Hebrews all cite Gen 15:6 and affirm both. E805, E806, E807, E829, E753, E754, E797, E801 Three NT authors cite the same OT figure and text, each affirming both faith and obedience. Neutral cmd-15 N119 The word apeitheo (G544) means both to disobey and to disbelieve, indicating unbelief and disobedience are linguistically inseparable. Word study: apeitheo G544 The dual translation is a lexical fact. Heb 3:18/19 parallel is stated in the text. Neutral cmd-15 N120 The phrase obedience of faith (hupakoe pisteos) forms the bookends of Romans (1:5; 16:26). E743, E745 The phrase appears at both the opening and closing of Romans. The bookend placement is a structural fact. Neutral cmd-15 N121 Jesus rejects workers of anomia (Mat 7:23), John defines sin as anomia (1 Jhn 3:4), Paul says Christ redeems from anomia (Tit 2:14). The same word identifies what is rejected, what constitutes sin, and what Christ redeems from. E782, E812, E777 Three texts use the same Greek word (anomia) in linked contexts. The lexical connection is stated. Neutral cmd-15 N122 The integration chain faith-love-law is established: faith works by love (Gal 5:6), love = keeping commandments (1 Jhn 5:3), love fulfills the law (Rom 13:10). E816, E814, cmd-12 E632 Each link is an explicit statement with shared vocabulary. The chain follows without adding concepts. Neutral cmd-15 N123 Rom 8:4 explains how faith establishes the law (Rom 3:31): faith receives the Spirit (Gal 3:14), the Spirit fulfills the laws righteous requirement in believers. E742, E794, Gal 3:14 Three texts state: faith establishes law, Spirit fulfills laws righteousness, Spirit received through faith. Neutral cmd-15 N124 Synthesis: The new covenant writes the same law on a different medium. The possessive my law (torati) identifies pre-existing content; the verb kathab links stone-writing and heart-writing. E836, E839, cmd-13:N100 The possessive my identifies pre-existing content. The same verb describes both inscriptions. No reader could deny that the text claims the same law is written on a different surface. Neutral cmd-16 N125 Synthesis: Love fulfills the law by keeping its specific commandments. Paul names five Decalogue commands as loves content. John defines love as commandment-keeping using the copula estin. E838, E842, E837 Paul names commandments in the same sentence declaring love fulfills the law. John uses estin to define love as commandment-keeping. Content identification is stated. Neutral cmd-16 N126 Synthesis: The Spirit-love-law chain is established: Spirit produces love (Rom 5:5; Gal 5:22), love fulfills law (Rom 13:10), laws righteous requirement fulfilled in Spirit-walkers (Rom 8:4). E840, E838, E844 Each link is stated independently by Paul. No additional concept is required to connect them. Neutral cmd-16 N127 Synthesis: Faith and commandment-keeping are co-existing marks, not alternatives. Commandments of God and faith of Jesus paired with and. Faith establishes law. Faith without works is dead. E841, E843, E842 Multiple texts pair them with the conjunction and. Paul emphatically denies faith voids the law. No reader could deny the texts present both as required. Neutral cmd-16 N128 Synthesis: The word entole (G1785) provides lexical continuity for commandments from Jesus (Jhn 14:15), through Paul (Rom 7:12; 13:9), John (1 Jn 5:3), to Revelation (14:12; 22:14). E837, E838, E842, E843 Lexical fact verifiable from the Greek text. The same noun appears in all these contexts. Neutral cmd-16

docs.title: INFERENCES (I)
docs.text: ID Claim Type What Bible Actually Says Why Inference Criteria Classification First Appeared Also In I001 The Decalogue is distinguished from all other biblical legislation by a consistent multi-dimensional pattern spanning speaker, writer, medium, repository, boundary marker, naming, and audience I-A E1-E19, N1-N5 establish each individual dimension separately Systematizes seven individual textual observations into a unified multi-dimensional distinction framework 5 Neutral cmd-01 I002 The attributes of the law (holy, just, good, spiritual, perfect, sure, true, eternal) mirror God's own attributes, indicating the Decalogue reflects God's character I-A E20-E27 list the law's attributes; Scripture attributes holiness, justice, goodness, and eternality to God Combines law-attribute statements with God-attribute statements into a relational pattern 5 Neutral cmd-01 I003 The Decalogue spans the entire Bible from Genesis (Gen 26:5) to Revelation (Rev 22:14), indicating universal and perpetual scope I-A E51 Abraham kept commandments pre-Sinai; E1-E8 Sinai; E22-E27 Psalms on permanence; E45-E46 prophetic heart-writing; E42-E44 Jesus/Paul continuity; E39-E41 Revelation Synthesizes data points from across the entire canon into a single doctrinal statement 5 Neutral cmd-01 I004 Love is the animating principle of the Decalogue, with the first table expressing love for God and the second table expressing love for neighbor I-A E28 Jesus two love commands; E31 Paul quotes Decalogue as love's content; E32 all law fulfilled in love; E33 James royal law = love; E38 John love = keeping commandments Mapping first table = love God and second table = love neighbor systematizes multiple E/N items with the two-tablet structure 5 Neutral cmd-01 cmd-12 I005 The new covenant fulfills the Decalogue by internalizing it through the Spirit rather than replacing it with different content I-A E45 my law on hearts; E46 Hebrews quotes same; E47 stone to heart; E48 Spirit enables statute-keeping; E50 righteousness of law fulfilled in Spirit-walkers Synthesizes E45-E50 into a single theological framework of internalization rather than replacement 5 Neutral cmd-01 cmd-13, cmd-14 I006 The NT maintains a vocabulary distinction between entole (commandments including Decalogue) and dogma (ceremonial ordinances abolished), confirming the Decalogue's continuing authority I-A E39-E41 use entole for end-time commandment-keeping; Eph 2:15 and Col 2:14 use dogma for what was abolished Systematizes lexical data into a doctrinal conclusion about continuing authority 5 Neutral cmd-01 I008 The first commandment was operative before Sinai, during the patriarchal era. I-A Jacob commanded his household to put away strange gods (E143); Abraham built altars exclusively to YHWH (E147); Joshua said their fathers served other gods before Abraham was called (E144). The text records patriarchal obedience and disobedience to exclusive worship but does not quote the first commandment as a formal law before Sinai. Systematizing these pre-Sinai accounts into a doctrinal claim requires combining multiple episodes. 5 Neutral cmd-02 I009 Covetousness constitutes a violation of the first commandment because it is idolatry -- thus the commandment extends beyond literal idol worship to any disordered desire. I-A Paul states covetousness which is idolatry (E129) and covetous man who is an idolater (E130). The first commandment prohibits other gods (E068). Connecting Pauls NT equation of covetousness with idolatry to the OT first commandment requires systematization. 5 Neutral cmd-02 cmd-03, cmd-11 I010 Gods jealousy functions like a husbands protective claim on the marriage covenant, and idolatry is therefore spiritual adultery. I-A God is called jealous (qanna, E072, E074); the prophets use the marriage metaphor for Israels idolatry; 1Co 10:22 echoes Deu 32:21 (E120). Synthesizing the marriage metaphor with the divine attribute into a unified doctrine requires systematization. 5 Neutral cmd-02 cmd-03 I012 The phrase al panay in Exo 20:3 means in my presence at any time and in any respect because Gods presence is universal. I-A The Hebrew phrase means upon my face / before me (E069, E070). The commandment uses this phrase as an adverbial modifier (E069). Extending before my face to at any time and in any respect because God is everywhere requires combining the spatial metaphor with the theological premise of divine omnipresence not stated in Exo 20:3 itself. 5 Neutral cmd-02 I013 The second commandment permits non-worship representational art (decorative imagery, illustrative art) since the prohibition targets images made for religious devotion, not all visual representation. I-A Neutral cmd-03 I014 The generational consequences of Exo 20:5 describe the sociological and spiritual reality that idolatrous families transmit their practices to their children, producing a culture of God-rejection across generations. I-A Neutral cmd-03 I015 The commandment prohibits representations of God specifically, since the temunah positive uses (Num 12:8; Psa 17:15) and God-commanded images (cherubim representing heavenly beings) suggest the target is likenesses of God rather than all images universally. I-A Neutral cmd-03 I016 The eschatological image of the beast (Rev 13:14-15; 14:9) is the final historical manifestation of the second commandments violation, making the commandment relevant through the end of time. I-A Neutral cmd-03 I017 The third commandment applies to all who identify as Gods people (not just Israel), since bearing Gods name is a function of belonging to Him. I-A 5 Neutral cmd-04 I018 Jesus teaching Swear not at all (Mat 5:34) does not abolish the legitimacy of oaths but calls for such habitual truthfulness that oaths become unnecessary. I-A 5 Neutral cmd-04 I019 The eschatological blasphemy of Daniel 7:25, 2 Thessalonians 2:4, and Revelation 13:1,6 represents the ultimate form of third-commandment violation: claiming divine prerogatives while misrepresenting Gods character. I-A 5 Neutral cmd-04 I020 The Sabbath commandment has universal scope, extending to all humanity rather than being limited to ethnic Israel I-A E261 ger in commandment, E262 creation basis, E280 Isaiah invites nekar, E283 all flesh, E284 anthropos Systematizes separate textual observations into unified doctrinal statement about universal reach 5 Neutral cmd-05 I021 The creation basis (Gen 2:2-3 to Exo 20:11 to Mark 2:27) establishes the Sabbath as a pre-national creation-era institution, not merely Mosaic legislation I-A E262 commandment cites creation, E263-264 creation text, E268-271 pre-Sinai, E284 made for anthropos Synthesizes chronological data points into institutional characterization 5 Neutral cmd-05 I022 The remember (zakar) command in Exo 20:8 implies the Sabbath was already known to the hearers at Sinai, not newly introduced I-A E258 zakar = remember, E268-E271 pre-Sinai evidence Combines lexical meaning of zakar with pre-Sinai evidence to infer prior acquaintance 5 Neutral cmd-05 I023 The progressive scope expansion from ger (Exo 20:10) to ben-nekar (Isa 56:6) to all flesh (Isa 66:23) to anthropos (Mark 2:27) represents an intentional biblical pattern of universalizing the Sabbath I-A E261 ger, E279-280 nekar, E283 all flesh, E284 anthropos Connects four independent texts into intentional trajectory. All components in E/N; the trajectory is systematization 5 Neutral cmd-05 I024 NT records of Sabbath practice (Jesus custom, women rest, Paul manner, Gentile assemblies) demonstrate Sabbath observance continued as normative practice in the apostolic church I-A E286 Jesus custom, E289 women commandment, E290-294 Paul practice, E295 sabbatismos remains Systematizes multiple individual data points into characterization of church practice 5 Neutral cmd-05 I026 The fifth commandment serves as a bridge commandment between the first table (duties to God) and the second table (duties to neighbor), since it connects parental honor to divine honor through shared vocabulary and structural position. I-A Neutral cmd-06 I027 The OT penalty provisions (death for striking or cursing parents, stoning for persistent rebellion) indicate that the commandment carries the same gravity as offenses against God Himself. I-A Neutral cmd-06 I028 The Proverbs corpus develops the fifth commandment into a comprehensive wisdom ethic linking parental honor to personal flourishing, with dishonor leading to destruction. I-A Neutral cmd-06 I029 The Corban controversy establishes a permanent principle that human religious tradition cannot override Gods moral commandments, even when the tradition claims to serve God. I-A Neutral cmd-06 I030 Jesus own life provides a model for the compatibility of divine priority and parental honor: He acknowledged His Fathers business yet submitted to parents, established Gods priority yet cared for Mary from the cross. I-A Neutral cmd-06 I031 The sixth commandment prohibits a progressive spectrum of harm: from anger (heart), through contempt (speech), to physical killing (act) -- a unified prohibition covering every stage I-A E348 (Cains anger preceded murder), E349 (Simeon/Levis anger led to killing), E383 (Jesus: anger, raca, fool), E385/E386 (murders from heart), E394 (lusts to killing), E398 (hatred = murder) Each stage is stated in E items. The unified progressive spectrum systematizes individual statements into one framework. 5 Neutral cmd-07 I032 The sixth commandment is grounded in a theology of blood spanning the entire Bible: blood cries (Gen 4:10), blood is life (Gen 9:4), shedding demands blood (Gen 9:6), blood defiles (Num 35:33), God investigates blood (Psa 9:12), earth discloses blood (Isa 26:21) I-A E347 (blood cries), E344 (blood-for-blood), E364 (blood defiles land), E373 (God investigates blood), E381 (earth discloses blood) Each element is stated in E table. The unified theology of blood spanning the Bible systematizes them into one theological framework. 5 Neutral cmd-07 I033 Ratsach (H7523) has a broader semantic range than English murder but narrower than English kill -- it covers all unlawful human-on-human killing (both intentional and unintentional) while excluding animal killing, warfare, and judicial execution I-A E342 (commandment word), E355 (ratsach for unintentional), E356-E357 (ratsach for intentional), N054 (dual range), E350 (execution by different word muth Hophal) Each usage is verifiable. The precise boundaries of the semantic range (excluding war, animals, execution) is a systematization of the observable usage pattern. 5 Neutral cmd-07 I034 The sixth commandment implies a duty to actively protect human life (not merely to refrain from killing), since the Mosaic legislation requires preventive measures such as safety railings, restraining dangerous animals, and communal expiation for unsolved murders I-A E370 (safety railing), E353 (negligent ox owner), E369 (communal expiation for unsolved murder) Each protective measure is stated. The claim of a general duty to actively protect life systematizes three case-law applications into a broader principle. 5 Neutral cmd-07 I035 The LXX-NT linguistic chain (ratsach to phoneuo to all NT commandment citations) demonstrates unbroken continuity from the Hebrew Decalogue through the Greek NT I-A E342 (ratsach in Exo 20:13), E382 (phoneuo in Mat 5:21), E387-E388 (phoneuo in Synoptics), E390 (phoneuo in Rom 13:9), E393 (phoneuo in Jas 2:11); word study: LXX translates ratsach as phoneuo 25 times Each citation is verifiable from the Greek text. The claim of unbroken continuity from Exodus to Revelation systematizes the lexical data into a historical-linguistic thesis. 5 Neutral cmd-07 I036 The seventh commandment, though using the narrow term naaph (adultery proper), implies a comprehensive sexual ethic covering all forms of sexual sin outside the one-flesh marriage of Gen 2:24. I-A E407 uses naaph. E413-E414 expand to 12+ categories. E423 extends to lustful intent. E432 addresses homosexual acts. E440 commands flight from all porneia. E449 names both pornoi and moichoi under judgment. Each individual expansion is explicit. The claim that the narrow commandment implies a comprehensive sexual ethic systematizes all these expansions into a single doctrine. 5 Neutral cmd-08 I037 The sexual ethic traces a consistent arc from creation through the Decalogue, Mosaic legislation, Proverbs, the Prophets, Jesus, the apostolic writings, to Revelation -- with no biblical author departing from this trajectory. I-A E409 (creation), E407-E408 (Decalogue), E413-E414 (Lev 18), E419-E421 (Proverbs), E422 (Malachi), E457 (Jeremiah), E423-E431 (Jesus), E432-E448 (Paul), E449-E451 (other NT), E452 (Jude), E453-E455 (Revelation). Each passage is individually explicit. The claim of a consistent arc with no departure systematizes data points from across the entire canon. 5 Neutral cmd-08 I038 Marriage is presented as a divine covenant institution, not merely a social contract. God established it at creation (E409), calls Himself Israels husband (E457), calls it a covenant through Malachi (E422), Jesus says God hath joined together (E425), and Paul grounds the body in divine ownership (E441). I-A E409, E422, E425, E441, E457 each state an aspect of marriages divine character. The claim that marriage is a divine covenant institution synthesizes these statements into a unified theological framework. All vocabulary comes from E/N tables. 5 Neutral cmd-08 I039 The body-temple theology provides the theological foundation for the seventh commandment in the NT era. The body is the temple of the Holy Spirit (E441), joined to Christ (E439), bought with a price (E441), therefore must flee fornication (E440). I-A E439, E440, E441 each state a distinct theological truth. The claim that these form the theological foundation for the commandment systematizes them into a doctrinal framework. 5 Neutral cmd-08 I040 The prophetic use of adultery/whoredom as a metaphor for Israels spiritual unfaithfulness presupposes and reinforces the literal seventh commandment. Jeremiah describes God as Israels husband and idolatry as adultery (E457). The figurative usage derives its force from the literal prohibition. I-A E457 and E379 each use the metaphor. The figurative use connects multiple passages with the literal prohibition. The claim that figurative use presupposes and reinforces the literal commandment connects multiple figurative usages to form a doctrinal statement. 5 Neutral cmd-08 I042 The eighth commandment establishes a comprehensive ethic of property and personhood: a hierarchy from absolute prohibition (taking persons = death) through graduated restitution (taking property = 2x-5x), economic integrity (just weights), labor justice (fair wages), and religious obligation (tithes to God). I-A Neutral cmd-09 I043 The eighth commandment connects to multiple other commandments: the 3rd (stealing profanes God's name, Pro 30:9), the 4th (Sabbath-breakers cheat in commerce, Amo 8:5), the 5th (robbing parents, Pro 28:24), the 7th (theft vs. adultery, Pro 6:30-35), the 9th (stealing linked to lying, Lev 19:11), and the 10th (coveting precedes stealing, Jos 7:21). I-A Neutral cmd-09 I044 The prophetic denunciations of theft (Jer 7:9; Hos 4:2; Amo 8:4-7; Mic 6:10-11; Zec 5:3-4; Mal 3:8) presuppose the continuing authority of the eighth commandment throughout Israel's history, because each prophet treats theft as a current covenant violation requiring judgment. I-A Neutral cmd-09 I045 The NT presents a transformation pattern for the eighth commandment: from prohibition (do not steal) to positive ethic (labor and share), paralleling the pattern of the 6th commandment (do not murder to love) and 7th commandment (do not commit adultery to marital purity). I-A Neutral cmd-09 I046 The shav/sheqer complementarity creates a comprehensive prohibition covering the entire spectrum of untruthful testimony -- from deliberate fabrication through careless, empty, or groundless claims -- forming a unified biblical theology of truthfulness I-A Neutral cmd-10 I047 The Bible presents truth and falsehood as a cosmic antithesis rooted in the natures of God and Satan: God cannot lie, Christ is truth, Christ had no guile, while the devil is the father of lies and devoid of truth I-A Neutral cmd-10 I048 The ninth commandment functions as a foundation for social order: its violation produces societal collapse (Isa 59:14), prophetic indictment (Hos 4:1-2), judicial murder (1 Ki 21; Mat 26:59), and eschatological exclusion (Rev 21:8; 22:15) I-A Neutral cmd-10 I049 The Rahab and midwives narratives show God blessing individuals who acted in faith to preserve life where deception also occurred, but the text commends their faith and life-preserving actions rather than the deception itself I-A Neutral cmd-10 I050 Pauls vice list in 1 Timothy 1:9-10 follows the Decalogue order (murderers=6th, whoremongers=7th, menstealers=8th, liars/perjurers=9th), demonstrating that the Decalogue structure governed NT moral reasoning I-A Neutral cmd-10 I051 The tenth commandment functions as the root from which all other Decalogue violations spring, because every external sin begins as internal desire. I-A Neutral cmd-11 I052 The Decalogue forms an inclusio -- from no other gods (1st commandment) to do not covet (10th commandment) -- because the NT equates covetousness with idolatry, linking the last commandment back to the first. I-A Neutral cmd-11 I053 Contentment is the positive expression of the first commandment: having no other gods means trusting God alone as sufficient, and contentment is that trust expressed in daily life. I-A Neutral cmd-11 I054 The three-fold taxonomy of worldly desire in 1 John 2:16 (lust of flesh, lust of eyes, pride of life) maps onto Eves temptation in Genesis 3:6 (good for food, pleasant to eyes, desired to make wise), establishing a consistent biblical framework for understanding the nature of covetous desire. I-A Neutral cmd-11 I055 Deuteronomy 5:21 expounds the single chamad of Exodus 20:17 into two semantic dimensions: the attractional pull toward a person (chamad for wife) and the acquisitive longing for possessions (hitavveh for property). I-A Neutral cmd-11 I056 The love-obedience formula is a unitary biblical concept spanning from the Decalogue (Exo 20:6) to Revelation (Rev 14:12), maintained by multiple authors across approximately 1,500 years without variation. I-A Neutral cmd-12 I057 Love does not replace the commandments but expresses itself through commandment-keeping. Love is the motive and the commandments are the expression. I-A Neutral cmd-12 I058 The new covenant internalizes the Decalogue through Spirit-enabled love rather than replacing it with different content. The change is in mode of enablement, not in moral content. I-A Neutral cmd-12 I059 Love reflects the character of God and is the means by which believers reflect God's character. Since God is love, the law reflects God's character, and love fulfills the law, love-motivated obedience images God. I-A Neutral cmd-12 cmd-13 I061 If Christ was the pre-incarnate divine person present with Israel, then my commandments in John 14:15 may carry the force of authorial ownership over the Decalogue. I-A Systematizes multiple E/N items 5 Neutral cmd-17-if-you-love-me-keep-my-commandments I062 My commandments in John 14:15 includes both the Decalogue and the love command as one unified set. I-A Systematizes multiple E/N items 5 Neutral cmd-17-if-you-love-me-keep-my-commandments I063 The seven-stage progressive revelation arc (pre-Sinai foundations, Sinai codification, case law application, prophetic expansion, Jesus's treatment, apostolic application, eschatological resolution) represents a unified biblical trajectory for the Decalogue from Genesis to Revelation. I-A Each stage is documented by E/N items across the twelve studies Systematizes multiple E/N items into a broader pattern 5 Neutral cmd-16 I064 The Decalogue's two-table structure (love God / love neighbor), bridged by the 5th commandment's use of divine-honor vocabulary (kabed, yare) for parents, constitutes an intentional literary design. I-A The two-table summary is explicit (Mat 22:37-40; Rom 13:8-10). The bridge vocabulary is explicit (kabed/yare for both God and parents). Intentional design requires systematization beyond what any single text states 5 Neutral cmd-16 I065 Every commandment has both a negative prohibition and a positive counterpart that emerges from the broader canonical treatment (e.g., murder/self-sacrificial love, stealing/giving, coveting/contentment). I-A Each individual negative-to-positive pairing is documented across the studies Universalizing from individual observations to a pattern covering all ten commandments 5 Neutral cmd-16 I066 The commandment series (789 items) and the law series (826 items) independently converge on the same conclusion: at the explicit and necessary implication tiers, the Bible presents the Decalogue as continuing in authority with no passage explicitly abolishing it. I-A The cmd series found no abolition text across 12 studies. The law series found 219 Continues, 0 Abolished at E+N tier. Convergence of two independent series is a synthesizing observation 5 Neutral cmd-16 I067 The Spirit enables comprehensive commandment-keeping, not just selected commandments. The Spirit produces the full spectrum of character required by the Decalogue: love for God, love for neighbor, self-control, and all virtues in the fruit of the Spirit. I-A Spirit causes walking in my statutes (E048). Fruit of Spirit: love, joy, peace, etc. (E633). All the law fulfilled in love (E032). Love fulfills the law (E733). N108 (flesh violations = Decalogue violations; Spirit fruit = law-compatible). N111 (Spirit-love fulfills law). Each individual statement is explicit. The claim that the Spirit enables comprehensive commandment-keeping covering all ten commandments systematizes the plural my statutes, the fruit list, and the all the law language into a unified doctrinal statement. 5 (systematizing) Neutral cmd-14 I068 The Spirit-flesh conflict (Gal 5:16-17; Rom 8:5-8) is the NT expression of the stony-heart/heart-of-flesh transition (Eze 36:26). The stony heart corresponds to the carnal mind that cannot submit to the law; the heart of flesh corresponds to the Spirit-minded person who fulfills the law's righteousness. I-A E661 (stony heart -> heart of flesh). E680 (carnal mind cannot submit to law). E050 (Spirit fulfills law). E047 (stone -> heart). N105 (Spirit resolves mismatch). The individual texts are explicit. The claim that the flesh-Spirit conflict is the NT expression of Ezekiel's heart-transformation systematizes Paul's framework with Ezekiel's promise. 5 (systematizing) Neutral cmd-14 I069 The Spirit fulfills the law in believers through a multi-faceted operation: heart-writing, love-production, flesh-mortification, progressive transformation, and teaching/convicting. I-A E047 (Spirit writes on hearts). E672 (Spirit witnesses to laws). E631 (love shed abroad by Spirit). E633 (fruit of Spirit). E700 (through Spirit mortify deeds). E677 (changed glory to glory). E709 (Spirit teaches). E711 (Spirit reproves of sin). E712 (Spirit guides into truth). Each individual operation is stated in the text. The claim of a multi-faceted operation systematizes five distinct Spirit-activities into a unified framework of law-fulfillment. 5 (systematizing) Neutral cmd-14 I070 The Spirit's role in commandment-keeping follows a consistent trajectory from OT promise to NT fulfillment: Eze 36:27 (Spirit causes obedience) -> Joel 2:28 (Spirit outpoured) -> Acts 2 (Pentecost) -> Rom 8:4 (law fulfilled in Spirit-walkers) -> 1 Jhn 3:24 (Spirit and commandments linked) -> Rev 14:12 (end-time commandment-keeping). I-A E048 (Eze 36:27). E685 (Joel 2:28). E050 (Rom 8:4). E715 (1 Jhn 3:24). Each passage is explicit. The claim of a consistent trajectory systematizes passages from different authors, periods, and genres into a single redemptive-historical arc. 5 (systematizing) Neutral cmd-14 I073 The Bible presents a consistent three-part pattern across multiple authors: (1) salvation is by grace/faith apart from works as the ground; (2) genuine faith necessarily produces obedience as its fruit; (3) faith and commandment-keeping are complementary, not contradictory. I-A Multiple authors state justification is by faith not works (E741, E774, E778, E834), works are fruit of faith (E751, E757, E775, E776, E780), and faith/commandments belong together (E742, E790, E814, E797). N115 distinguishes ground from fruit; N116 shows faith-obedience inseparable across authors. Each individual statement is explicit. The claim that these constitute a consistent three-part pattern across multiple authors systematizes individual texts from Paul, James, John, Jesus, Hebrews, and Peter into a unified framework. All components are from E/N tables. #5 (systematizing) Neutral cmd-15 I074 The obedience of faith (Rom 1:5; 16:26) refers to obedience that consists in faith, springs from faith, and responds to the gospel -- a concept in which faith and obedience are inseparable rather than sequential. Abrahams by faith...obeyed (Heb 11:8) illustrates this simultaneity. I-A E743 (Rom 1:5: obedience to the faith). E745 (Rom 16:26: obedience of faith). E797 (Heb 11:8: by faith...obeyed). N120 (bookends of Romans). Word study: hupakoe G5218 = hearing under. Each text is explicit. The claim that faith and obedience are inseparable rather than sequential interprets the genitive relationship in hupakoe pisteos by combining the lexical evidence with the Abraham illustration. All components are from E/N tables and word study. #5 (systematizing) Neutral cmd-15 I075 Paul and James do not contradict each other on justification. Paul addresses the GROUND of justification (faith, not works-merit: Rom 3:28; 4:2-5), while James addresses the EVIDENCE of justification (genuine faith produces works: Jas 2:14-26). Both cite Gen 15:6 and Abraham, affirming both his faith and his obedience. I-A E741 (Paul: justified by faith without law-works). E829-E830 (Paul: Abraham credited righteousness). E753-E755 (James: Abraham justified by works; not by faith only). E757 (James: faith without works = body without spirit). N118 (Abraham demonstrates both). Each authors statement is explicit. The claim that they address different questions synthesizes both sets of statements into a harmonized framework. All components are from E/N tables. Both authors cite the same text (Gen 15:6) and same figure (Abraham), which is the verified SIS connection (#4a). #5 (systematizing) Neutral cmd-15 I076 The faith-love-commandment-keeping-law-established chain, traced through Gal 5:6 to 1 Jhn 5:3 to Rom 13:10 to Rom 8:4 to Rom 3:31, represents the Bibles answer to how faith and commandment-keeping hold together: faith operates through Spirit-produced love, love keeps the commandments, and this fulfills the laws righteous requirement, thereby establishing the law. I-A E816 (Gal 5:6: faith works by love). E814 (1 Jhn 5:3: love = keeping commandments). E818 (Gal 5:14: love fulfills law). E794 (Rom 8:4: righteousness of law fulfilled in Spirit-walkers). E742 (Rom 3:31: faith establishes law). N122 (faith-love-law chain). N123 (faith-Spirit-law fulfilled). Each link is explicit. The claim that this chain represents the Bibles answer to the study question systematizes five explicit statements and two necessary implications into a comprehensive doctrinal framework. All vocabulary and concepts come from the E/N tables. #5 (systematizing) Neutral cmd-15 I077 Hebrews 11 demonstrates that biblical faith is inherently active: every instance of faith produces a corresponding obedient action. No faith-instance in the chapter is described as passive belief alone. I-A E797 (Abraham obeyed by faith). E798 (faith = substance/evidence). E799 (faith necessary for pleasing God). E800 (Noah prepared ark by faith). E801 (Abraham offered Isaac by faith). E802 (Moses chose suffering by faith). E803 (Rahab received spies by faith). E804 (faith-heroes wrought righteousness). Each verse is explicit about a faith-action. The claim that every instance is active and no instance is passive generalizes from the individual cases to a comprehensive pattern. The generalization is verifiable from the text (every by-faith clause in the chapter includes an action verb). All components from E/N tables. #5 (systematizing) Neutral cmd-15 I078 The distinction between works of the law as justification-ground (rejected) and good works as salvation-fruit (required) is maintained consistently across the Pauline corpus and harmonizes with James, John, and Jesus. The same word ergon (G2041) serves both constructions; context determines meaning. I-A E741, E765, E774, E778, E834 (works of law/works of righteousness rejected as ground). E775, E776, E777, E780 (good works as purpose/fruit). E751, E757 (James: faith without works dead). Word study: ergon G2041 used in both senses. Each statement about works is explicit. The claim of a consistent distinction maintained across the corpus systematizes multiple texts using the same word (ergon) in different senses into a unified lexical framework. All components from E/N tables and word studies. #5 (systematizing) Neutral cmd-15 I079 Grace is presented in Scripture as both forensic (declaring righteous: Rom 3:24; Tit 3:7) and transformative (teaching godly living: Tit 2:11-12; producing good works: Eph 2:10; empowering through the Spirit: Rom 8:4). Grace does not merely change the believers legal status but transforms the believers character and conduct. I-A E739 (justified freely by grace). E779 (justified by grace). E776 (grace teaches righteous living). E775 (created unto good works). E794 (righteousness of law fulfilled by Spirit). E777 (redeemed from anomia, zealous of good works). N115 (ground vs. fruit). Each statement about grace is explicit. The claim that grace is both forensic and transformative systematizes multiple grace-texts into a unified theology of grace. All components from E/N tables. #5 (systematizing) Neutral cmd-15 I080 The Bibles answer to both legalism (works-righteousness) and antinomianism (lawlessness) is the same: faith which worketh by love (Gal 5:6). Legalism is addressed by justification through faith apart from works (Rom 3:28; Gal 2:16). Antinomianism is addressed by the insistence that genuine faith produces obedience (Jas 2:17; Rom 6:1-2; Mat 7:21-23). Both errors are refuted from the same unified teaching. I-A E741, E765, E774 (against legalism: not justified by works). E742, E751, E758, E762, E781-E782, E790 (against antinomianism: faith establishes law; faith without works dead; grace does not license sin; workers of anomia rejected; commandments + faith). E816 (faith working by love as the integration). Each anti-legalism and anti-antinomianism statement is explicit. The claim that both errors are refuted from the same unified teaching systematizes the two sets into a comprehensive framework. All components from E/N tables. #5 (systematizing) Neutral cmd-15 I081 Synthesis: The Decalogue is a unified whole with internal architecture -- two tables (love God/love neighbor), external-to-internal trajectory (1-9 address actions; 10th addresses desire), and inclusio (1st/10th, covetousness = idolatry). I-A E836-E837 (divine origin on two tablets). E838 (Paul lists second-table under neighbor-love). cmd-11:N089 (covetousness = idolatry). Systematizes observations from across the series into a structural framework. 5 (systematizing) Neutral cmd-16 I082 Synthesis: The new covenant fulfills the Decalogue by internalizing it through the Spirit rather than replacing it with different content. Change is in mode (stone to heart, flesh to Spirit), not moral content. I-A E839-E840 (heart-writing, Spirit-enablement). N124-N126 (same law, Spirit chain). Synthesizes heart-writing, Spirit-enablement, and law-character texts into unified covenant-theology framework. 5 (systematizing) Neutral cmd-16 I083 Synthesis: The Spirit-love-law chain (Spirit->love->commandment-keeping->law fulfilled->law established) is the central mechanism of new covenant commandment-keeping, integrating cmd-12 through cmd-15. I-A E838-E844 (each link in the chain). N124-N128 (chain established across texts). Each link is stated independently. The claim that these form the central mechanism systematizes chain-links into unified soteriological-ethical framework. 5 (systematizing) Neutral cmd-16 I084 Synthesis: Every NT author who addresses the Decalogue treats it as a continuing moral standard -- Jesus affirms, Paul establishes, James names it royal law, John defines love/sin by it, Hebrews affirms heart-writing, Revelation identifies end-time saints. I-A E836-E846 (individual author statements). N124-N128 (synthesis implications). Each authors treatment is explicit. The claim of uniform NT treatment systematizes individual statements from multiple authors into a single continuity conclusion. 5 (systematizing) Neutral cmd-16 I085 Synthesis: The Decalogue spans the entire Bible from creation (Gen 2:2-3; 2:24; 9:6) through Sinai (Exo 20:1-17) to Jesus (Mat 5:17-28) to Paul/John (Rom 3:31; 1 Jn 5:3) to Revelation (Rev 14:12; 22:14). I-A Each data point is explicit across multiple studies (cmd-01 through cmd-15). The claim of spanning the entire Bible systematizes individual references from across the canon into a unified arc. 5 (systematizing) Neutral cmd-16 I086 Synthesis: The Bible refutes both legalism (works as salvation ground: Rom 3:24; Eph 2:8-9) and antinomianism (faith without obedience: Rom 3:31; Jas 2:17; Mat 7:23) with the same unified teaching: faith which worketh by love (Gal 5:6). I-A E841 (faith establishes law), E845 (workers of anomia rejected), cmd-15:E774-E835. Each refutation is stated independently. The claim that the same unified teaching refutes both errors systematizes anti-legalism and anti-antinomianism texts. 5 (systematizing) Neutral cmd-16 I087 Synthesis: Every commandment deepened to the heart by Jesus/NT: anger=murder (Mat 5:22), lust=adultery (Mat 5:28), covetousness=idolatry (Col 3:5). The 10th commandments internal focus anticipates Jesus heart-deepening of the entire Decalogue. I-A Each deepening is explicit in the texts (cmd-02 through cmd-11). Rom 7:7 identifies 10th commandment as the one exposing Pauls sin. The claim that the 10th commandment anticipates the whole heart-deepening pattern systematizes observations across all ten commandments. 5 (systematizing) Neutral cmd-16 I007 The schoolmaster function of the law (Gal 3:24) refers to the law's role in revealing sin and pointing to Christ, not to the abolition of the law's moral content I-B E60 law was schoolmaster unto Christ; E59 added till the seed; E42 not a jot passes; E44 faith establishes law; E25-E27 stand fast forever; E20-E21 holy just good spiritual; E39-E41 end-time commandment-keeping Some E items describe temporal limitation (E59-E60) while others affirm permanence (E42, E44, E25-E27). Choosing between these requires interpretation. 2 Neutral cmd-01 I011 The gods of Psalm 82 are human judges or rulers, not actual deities. I-B Psa 82:1 says God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods (E106). Psa 82:6-7 says I have said Ye are gods... But ye shall die like men (E107). Elohim (H430) is used 4 times for judges in the OT (E149). Some read gods as human judges (based on the die like men clause and judicial context); others read them as divine council members. The interpreter must choose between readings. 2 Neutral cmd-02 I025 Nehemiah 9:14 madest known describes formal revelation at Sinai rather than first introduction, given pre-Sinai evidence of Exo 16:4-30 I-B E299 madest known at Sinai. E268-271 pre-Sinai Sabbath. Reader must choose between possible meanings. E299 could mean first introduction or formal codification. Choosing requires weighing E268-271 against E299. 2 Neutral cmd-05 I041 The porneia exception clause in Mat 19:9 (E427) permits divorce and remarriage on the ground of sexual immorality, while the parallel accounts in Mark (E428) and Luke (E429) record no exception, presenting the teaching as absolute. I-B E424 and E427 state except it be for porneia. E428 and E429 contain no exception clause. E425 states let not man put asunder without qualification. E/N items exist on both sides. Matthew records an exception; Mark and Luke do not. This requires choosing between possible readings. 2 Neutral cmd-08 I071 Not under the law (Gal 5:18) means freedom from the law's condemning jurisdiction, not from its moral content. Spirit-led persons fulfill the law through love (Gal 5:14), avoid flesh-works that violate the law (Gal 5:19-21), and produce fruit against which there is no law (Gal 5:22-23). I-B FOR: E032 (all law fulfilled in love). E445 (works of flesh = violations). E633 (fruit of Spirit -- no law against). AGAINST: E706 (led by Spirit, not under law). Requires choosing between two possible readings of not under the law. Both sides cite textual evidence. Resolved Strong by SIS: immediate context (vv.14,19-21,22-23) treats law content as operative. 2 (choosing between readings) Neutral cmd-14 I072 The letter that kills (2 Cor 3:6) and ministration of death (2 Cor 3:7) refer to the old covenant administration of the law, not the law itself. The same law that kills when administered through flesh gives life when administered through Spirit. I-B FOR: E681 (law holy, just, good). E021 (law spiritual). E675 (ministration of death was glorious). E679 (law weak through flesh). AGAINST: E674 (letter killeth). E675 (ministration of death on stones). Requires interpreting the letter killeth as statement about administration rather than law's inherent character. Both readings cite textual evidence. Resolved Strong by SIS: Paul calls the same law holy, just, good, spiritual. 2 (choosing between readings) Neutral cmd-14

docs.title: Ten Commandments Deep Dive Series — Methodology
docs.text: This file defines the methodology for ALL studies in the cmd-XX series (Ten Commandments Deep Dive). Every analysis agent MUST follow this methodology.

docs.title: Central Question
docs.text:
What does the Bible say about each of the Ten Commandments?
